sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-HA western blot (SDS-PAGE) confirmed strong expression of full-length HA-tagged GPR84 in CHO-HA-hGPR84 clone #7F12; weaker expression in clones #3E11 and CHO-HA-mGPR84 #18E7. No HA signal in untagged commercial CHO-hGPR84 (DiscoverX) or parental CHO-K1 cells. Functional assay result NOT MEASURED in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: GPR84 is a GPCR with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–21 extracellularly, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus. An N-terminal HA tag therefore prepends before M1 (insert_after_residue = 0), confirmed by Python: residue_after = seq[0] = 'M'. The 21-residue extracellular N-terminal domain provides ample clearance from TM1 (which begins at residue 22). L1 explicitly states the coding sequence is 'preceded by an N-terminal HA-tag in a Kozak setting'; L2 and L3 confirm the tag enables surface antibody recognition and is detected by western blot in the full-length membrane-anchored receptor. Full-length human GPR84 coding sequence preceded by an N-terminal HA-tag in a Kozak setting, stably expressed in CHO cells (CHO-HA-hGPR84 clones). The same construct was made for mouse GPR84. The HA tag was used to confirm surface expression by antibody recognition.

sources.claim: Gene fragments containing Homo sapiens (NCBI Reference Sequence: NM_020370.3 ) and Mus musculus (NCBI Reference Sequence: NM_030720.3 , codon optimised) ( O'Leary et al., 2016 ) GPR84 coding sequences preceded by an N-terminal HA-tag in a Kozak setting and flanked by restriction enzyme sites for AflII and XbaI were designed using SnapGene® software (from Insightful Science; available at snapgene.com ) and synthesised by Twist Biosciences (San Francisco, CA).

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the same experimental construct and are consolidated into one site grounded on L1. No residue number is explicitly named in any clip; the position is derived from the topology (no signal peptide, single extracellular N-terminus). No internal loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or other positions appear anywhere in the ledger for GPR84. The validation level is surface_only because the clips confirm expression and antibody detection of the surface receptor but do not report a functional (e.g., signalling or ligand-binding) assay on the HA-tagged construct.
